hypotheses.justification: It follows from `[Module (ZMod p) Bc]`. By `Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/NatInt.lean) we get `p • b = ((p : ZMod p)) • b`, and `(p : ZMod p) = 0` (`ZMod.natCast_self`), so `p • b = 0 • b = 0`. The proof uses `hB` once, in `hpx`; there it can be replaced by `fun b => by rw [← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul (ZMod p), ZMod.natCast_self, zero_smul]`. This deletion and the deletion of `[Module (ZMod p) Bc]` (next entry) are alternatives: each can go on its own, but not both.

This is a binder of the theorem, not a `variable`. Nothing else in the statement uses it: `p • b` in `hB` is ℕ-smul. It can be rebuilt from `hB` with `AddCommGroup.zmodModule hB` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/ZMod.lean), via `letI`. The proof only uses facts that hold for any `ZMod p`-module structure: the basis `Module.Basis.ofVectorSpace`, and `Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul`, which holds for every module structure. So the same proof goes through. This deletion and the deletion of `hB` are alternatives, not both together.

The conclusion does not mention `Bc` or `ε`. Without surjectivity, apply the theorem to the corestriction `ε' : P →ₗ[ℤ] LinearMap.range ε` (`LinearMap.rangeRestrict`), which is surjective. It has the same kernel as `ε`, so `Function.Exact ι ε'` still holds. `LinearMap.range ε` is finite, as a subtype of a finite type. It is p-torsion, because `hB` restricts to it. It gets a `ZMod p`-module structure from `AddCommGroup.zmodModule`. The theorem for `ε'` then gives the same conclusion. Equivalently, in the proof take the basis of the range of `ε` and lift its elements, instead of lifting a basis of `Bc`.

Finiteness is only used to make the basis index set a `Fintype`, so that `Fintype.linearCombination` and finite sums can be used. For prime p, `Bc` is an `F_p`-vector space and always has a basis `bB`, possibly infinite. The same argument works with `Finsupp` in place of functions. Take `s : R × (I →₀ ℤ) → P`, `(r, c) ↦ ι r + Finsupp.linearCombination ℤ x c`, and `χ₀` likewise with `e'`. Surjectivity of `s`: write `bB.repr (ε y)`, a finsupp, and lift its coefficients to ℤ. Kernel containment: from `ι r + Σ c_i x_i = 0`, applying `ε` and using linear independence of `bB` gives `p ∣ c_i`. Then injectivity of `ι` gives `r = -Σ m_i rr_i`, and `χ₀` vanishes exactly as before. The lift through `quotKerEquivOfSurjective` is unchanged. So the statement holds without `[Finite Bc]`, as long as `hp` is kept.

The statement stays true for every p, with `[Finite Bc]` kept. p = 0: `hu` forces `u r = 0 • e' = 0`, so `χ = 0` works. p = 1: `Bc` is trivial, `ι` is bijective by exactness and `hε`, and `χ = u ∘ ι⁻¹`. p ≥ 2: by `AddCommGroup.equiv_directSum_zmod_of_finite` (Mathlib/GroupTheory/FiniteAbelian/Basic.lean), `Bc` is a finite direct sum of cyclic groups. They have generators `b_i` of orders `d_i`, and `d_i ∣ p` by `hB`. Lift each `b_i` to `x_i ∈ P`. Exactness gives `d_i • x_i = ι(r_i)`, and `hu` gives `u(r_i) = p • e'_i`. Define `χ₀ : R × (I → ℤ) → E'` by `(r, c) ↦ u r + Σ c_i (p/d_i) • e'_i`, and `s` as in the proof; `s` is surjective just as before. If `ι r + Σ c_i x_i = 0`, applying `ε` gives `d_i ∣ c_i`, say `c_i = d_i m_i`. Injectivity of `ι` gives `r = -Σ m_i r_i`. Then `χ₀(r, c) = -Σ m_i p e'_i + Σ m_i p e'_i = 0`. So `χ₀` factors through `P`, and it extends `u`. Only the basis step of the proof changes (cyclic decomposition instead of an `F_p`-basis), and nothing else in the statement needs primality: `ZMod p` is a ring for every p. Deleting both this and `[Finite Bc]` together is not claimed.
